skybridge.boundary: This clean worktree base is not the current dirty product tree and is not integrated-system evidence.

q_periapt.boundary: Component proofs and release artifacts remain upstream evidence and do not establish BoundSessionV1.

claims.title: BoundSessionContextV1 has one canonical, prefix-free encoding
claims.claim: All supported implementations encode and reject BoundSessionContextV1 identically.
claims.boundary: The field set and rejection rules are specified, but no normative codec, vectors, or differential execution exists.
negative_evidence: No integrated Rust codec exists.
No independent decoder or cross-language vector set exists.

claims.title: Every product handshake decision originates at the trusted policy boundary
claims.claim: A business-capable handshake cannot use a decision forged or re-selected outside the trusted policy boundary.
claims.boundary: The current component ABI decision is a trusted-caller value, not an authorization capability against hostile same-process code.
negative_evidence: No isolated policy service or equivalent capability owner has been implemented.
Existing product selection and signed-policy paths are separate control planes.

claims.title: Policy state is monotonic across concurrency, crash, and restart
claims.claim: Within a fixed trust-root namespace, accepted policy state cannot regress or accept equal-version equivocation.
claims.boundary: Whole-device rollback, store deletion, and global freshness require an external witness or stronger platform assumption.
negative_evidence: No integrated crash/restart state model exists.
Policy update semantics for active sessions are undefined.

claims.title: Each local decision authorizes the exact caller, peer, purpose, owner, and local effect scope
claims.claim: A trusted policy service creates a session decision only when its policy snapshot authorizes the authenticated caller, expected peer, canonical PurposeV1, current LocalOwnerBinding, and endpoint-private typed LocalEffectScopeSet.
claims.boundary: A peer signature proves an endpoint assertion, not remote hardware attestation or execution of the asserted policy.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 policy service, local-effect-scope authority, or purpose-authorization model exists.
The current component decision does not bind a product peer, purpose, or local owner.

claims.title: Each local decision refines to one compliant local provider for the agreed wire profile
claims.claim: After a local decision is created, no other product path re-selects its protocol version, suite, hybrid profile, key format, or provider, and the selected provider implements the agreed wire profile.
claims.boundary: The protocol establishes agreement on wire cryptographic semantics; it does not prove that heterogeneous peers execute byte-identical providers.
negative_evidence: Existing signed-policy and product provider-selection paths remain separate authorities.
No final provider-to-wire traceability proof exists.

claims.title: Untrusted local callers cannot forge, transfer, replay, or widen a decision handle
claims.claim: The trusted service authenticates the IPC caller and binds each non-serializable server-side handle to a principal, peer, purpose, owner, local effect scope, epoch, expiry, and one-time operation sequence.
claims.boundary: An honest-host same-process implementation does not satisfy this claim; OS or trusted-service compromise remains out of scope.
negative_evidence: No isolated service, authenticated IPC protocol, or server-side BoundSession handle table exists.

claims.title: Accepted effects agree injectively on the peer-visible session and bilateral authorization tuple
claims.claim: Every accepted purpose-specific effect has one unique matching peer run over the same policy, wire profile, purpose, context, transcript, peer session, shared grant, bilateral-ready digest, and key identity, plus a separately authorized local decision and owner transaction.
claims.boundary: Local provider and owner identities are endpoint-private; existing component models use different message grammars and cannot be combined as this theorem.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 Tamarin theory exists.
No anti-vacuity or field-removal controls exist.

claims.title: The integrated session key remains secret if either hybrid component remains secure
claims.claim: Under explicit identity and component-compromise conditions, an active network attacker does not learn the BoundSessionV1 root key when one PQ/T component holds.
claims.boundary: Upstream combiner binding is not an AKE secrecy theorem, and no complete computational AKE proof is claimed.
negative_evidence: No integrated secrecy theorem exists.
A static Q suite does not provide forward secrecy after KEM private-key compromise.

claims.title: A policy-bound PQ/T attempt cannot yield a business-capable classic session
claims.claim: Network, timeout, overload, cancellation, parse, identity, ABI, and provider failures terminate a policy-bound attempt without business fallback.
claims.boundary: A separately identified compatibility protocol may exist, but its declaration authenticates an endpoint assertion rather than proving a local failure fact.
negative_evidence: No single product authority currently covers both signed policy and provider/fallback selection.

claims.title: Keys and grants for one purpose cannot authorize another purpose or channel
claims.claim: The key schedule, grant, channel API, and receipt authentication separate purposes, logical channels, roles, and directions.
claims.boundary: Purpose separation does not establish metadata privacy or safety after endpoint compromise.
negative_evidence: No integrated purpose-separated key schedule, grant type, or negative cross-purpose corpus exists.

claims.title: Only the exact current local owner can commit and publish a grant
claims.claim: The authorization transaction and the later bilateral-enable transaction each compare-and-swap caller principal, connection generation, operation token, driver identity, arbiter lease, and decision epoch before a grant can be published.
claims.boundary: The peer-agreed session identifier is distinct from each endpoint's private local owner generation.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 transaction or crash/ABA state model exists.

claims.title: The exact local authorization record is transactionally stored before grant publication
claims.claim: A BoundSessionGrant cannot be published or used until one local transaction validates the exact owner and stores both the pending authorized grant state and matching diagnostic authorization record, followed by a distinct owner-validated bilateral-enable transition.
claims.boundary: The record means local grant authorization, not application success; it is not durable, non-repudiable, or root-resistant without separately evidenced storage and witnesses.
negative_evidence: The current product success path resumes its caller before beginning the audit session.
The current established event routes under a redacted identifier rather than the new exact session chain.

claims.title: Both endpoints authenticate one shared grant and bilateral-ready set before local enablement
claims.claim: Each endpoint persists monotonic authorization/ready/enable states, derives the same domain-separated sharedGrantId, authenticates both role-ordered GrantReadyV1 values, stores one bilateralReadyDigest, and revalidates its private local owner immediately before enabling the grant.
claims.boundary: Local grant identifiers, decision epochs, authorization transaction identifiers, and owner bindings remain endpoint-private; a peer ready value authenticates a service assertion rather than remotely attesting its implementation or storage.
negative_evidence: No bilateral-ready state model, normative codec, integrated implementation, or replay/crash corpus exists.

claims.title: Untrusted application code cannot mint a successful application-effect receipt
claims.claim: Only a sealed PresentationCommitter, InputCommitter, or DurableFileCommitter can consume a one-use operation capability for an authorized LocalEffectScopeSet target, execute or directly verify the named platform completion event, and authorize the receipt service to MAC its derived canonical outcome.
claims.boundary: A software completion event does not prove human perception, a later physical consequence, remote hardware state, or durability stronger than the named platform primitive.
negative_evidence: No isolated effect committer, authenticated outcome channel, protected receipt-key path, or effect-bound negative corpus exists.

claims.title: Every accepted purpose receipt corresponds to the exact authenticated application effect
claims.claim: A verified receipt binds sharedGrantId, bilateralReadyDigest, the issuer authorization commitment, purpose, context, transcript, role-relative direction, operation identifier, monotonic sequence, trusted result, and effect digest to one uniquely journaled application effect.
claims.boundary: A missing receipt after a potentially applied operation is ambiguous; network submission or an authorization record is not application success.
negative_evidence: No normative receipt codec, state model, idempotency store, or final-device effect capture exists.

claims.title: Final implementations conform to the normative encodings and modeled enforcement points
claims.claim: Rust, C, Swift, and Kotlin faces produce identical normative values and enforce the modeled checks at mapped code boundaries.
claims.boundary: KATs, differential tests, source hashes, and traceability are not a mechanized specification-to-binary refinement theorem.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 implementation or cross-language corpus exists.

claims.title: The final integrated hybrid implementation passes two-ISA binary constant-time discrimination
claims.claim: Final release binaries on x86-64 and aarch64 produce zero genuine-secret findings while detecting the planted-leak positive control.
claims.boundary: Dynamic discrimination is not a complete constant-time proof or coverage of every platform and microarchitecture.
negative_evidence: Existing component captures are historical relative to later backend or source changes.

claims.title: Final-source Apple endpoints complete purpose-bound physical-device sessions
claims.claim: Named physical Apple endpoints complete authenticated BoundSessionV1 handshakes and bidirectional purpose-specific receipts from final-source binaries.
claims.boundary: Build, simulator, primitive benchmark, discovery, and TCP reachability evidence do not satisfy this claim.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 physical-device run exists.

claims.title: A real non-Apple endpoint interoperates with the same final protocol core
claims.claim: At least one physical or bare-metal non-Apple endpoint completes the same authenticated wire protocol and application receipts with an Apple endpoint.
claims.boundary: Static contract checks, cross-compilation, package construction, emulator-only checks, and TCP payload proxies are insufficient.
negative_evidence: No final BoundSessionV1 non-Apple endpoint exists.

claims.title: Remote desktop success is bound to trusted presentation completion and owner-authenticated control receipt
claims.claim: A remote desktop trial succeeds only after the intended endpoint's trusted renderer observes the defined presentation completion and, for interactive mode, the trusted input committer returns an authenticated OS-acceptance receipt for an owner-bound control action.
claims.boundary: UI connected state, a local socket, a decoded synthetic frame, one-way control submission, human perception, and later physical consequences are outside this completion claim.
negative_evidence: No purpose-bound final-source trial exists.

claims.title: File-transfer success is bound to direction, length, content digest, and durable receiver receipt
claims.claim: A file-transfer trial succeeds only after the receiver durably commits the declared bytes and returns an authenticated matching SHA-256 receipt.
claims.boundary: Network submission, sender completion, or receiver memory buffering is not durable success.
negative_evidence: No BoundSessionV1 file-transfer trial exists.

claims.title: Purpose binding has bounded cost against matched hybrid baselines
claims.claim: On predeclared primary metrics, the final integrated system stays within application-relevant non-inferiority margins against matched final-source PQ/T baselines.
claims.boundary: Single-host primitive timings, unmatched endpoints, historical backends, and failure to reject a null hypothesis do not establish non-inferiority.
negative_evidence: No final protocol, margins, or matched raw measurements exist.

claims.title: All submitted claims and results bind to one immutable evidence root
claims.claim: Every theorem, test, binary, device run, raw sample, table, and figure is selected by one final immutable source and evidence manifest.
claims.boundary: A local clean worktree or hash list alone is not a remote trust anchor, binary attestation, or independently reproduced result.
negative_evidence: No final implementation or evidence manifest exists.

claims.title: The research has been submitted or published
claims.claim: A submission or publication record exists for this independent manuscript.
claims.boundary: Drafting, local compilation, preprints, and repository branches are not peer-reviewed publication.
negative_evidence: The manuscript is not submission-ready and has not been submitted.
